question: A nurse caring for a woman on the postnatal ward notes that her legs are swollen and painful 3 days after delivery. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put a warm pack on and then wait
option_2: Massage the leg to ease the pain
option_3: Ask her to walk around the ward
option_4: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A swollen painful leg 3 days after delivery points to a deep vein clot, so the leg is kept still and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: a swollen painful leg after delivery

Priority Principle: Deep vein thrombosis

Why Not Others: (a) A warm pack does not treat the danger; (b) Massage may break off the clot; (c) Walking may move the clot to the lung.

PGI Exam Trap: The leg is massaged to ease the pain.

5-Second Recall: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen leg after birth means a clot.

question: A nurse on the ward sees a colleague share a woman's private details with a person who is NOT in the care team. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell other patients about it
option_2: Ignore it as a small matter
option_3: Report the breach to the senior nurse
option_4: Blame the colleague in front of all
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report the breach to the senior nurse

Clinical Rationale: Patient details are private, so a breach is reported to the senior nurse, who can put it right in the proper way.

Key Clue: a colleague who shares private details

Priority Principle: Confidentiality breach

Why Not Others: (a) Telling others spreads the breach; (b) Ignoring it lets the breach go on; (d) Public blame is not the proper way.

PGI Exam Trap: The breach is ignored as a small matter.

5-Second Recall: Report the breach to the senior nurse.

PNC Exam Pearl: A privacy breach is reported.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the kidneys is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: They pump the blood around the body
option_2: They filter the blood and make urine
option_3: They make the bile that digests fat
option_4: They take in the air for breathing
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) They filter the blood and make urine

Clinical Rationale: The kidneys filter the waste from the blood and make urine, so the body keeps the right balance of fluid and salts.

Key Clue: the work of the kidneys

Priority Principle: Kidney function

Why Not Others: (a) The heart pumps the blood; (c) Bile is made in the liver; (d) The lungs take in the air.

PGI Exam Trap: The bile that digests fat is made in the kidneys.

5-Second Recall: They filter the blood and make urine.

PNC Exam Pearl: Kidneys filter and make urine.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has just had a chest tube removed notes that he becomes breathless with air leaking from the wound. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help
option_2: Ask him to take a deep breath and lie flat
option_3: Leave the site and note it for the round
option_4: Give him a hot drink and let him rest
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help

Clinical Rationale: Breathlessness with air leaking from the wound after a chest tube is out points to air entering the chest, so a sterile dressing is pressed on and help called.

Key Clue: a small crackle of air at the wound after a chest tube

Priority Principle: Air leak

Why Not Others: (b) Lying flat may worsen his breathing; (c) Leaving the site lets air enter the chest; (d) A hot drink does not stop the air leak.

PGI Exam Trap: The site is left alone and noted for the round.

5-Second Recall: Press a sterile dressing on the site and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Air at the wound means press and call.

question: A community nurse visits a home where a man with a long term illness is on the same medicine for many months without a review. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell him to stop all medicine at once
option_2: Review his medicine with the doctor and check his progress
option_3: Ask him to double every dose at home
option_4: Leave the medicine and take no action
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Review his medicine with the doctor and check his progress

Clinical Rationale: A long term medicine needs a proper review, so the nurse checks it with the doctor and looks at the man's progress.

Key Clue: a man on the same medicine for months without review

Priority Principle: Medicine review

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping all medicine at once may harm him; (c) Doubling doses at home is dangerous; (d) Taking no action leaves him unreviewed.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is told to stop all his medicine at once.

5-Second Recall: Review his medicine with the doctor and check his progress.

PNC Exam Pearl: Old medicine needs a fresh review.

question: A nurse caring for an elderly woman on the ward who has fallen notes that one leg is shorter and turned out. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Try to straighten the leg by hand
option_2: Ask her to stand and walk to test the leg
option_3: Keep her still and call for help at once
option_4: Help her up and put her in bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep her still and call for help at once

Clinical Rationale: A leg that is shorter and turned out after a fall points to a broken hip, so the woman is kept still and help called at once.

Key Clue: a leg that is shorter and turned out after a fall

Priority Principle: Broken hip

Why Not Others: (a) Straightening by hand may cause more harm; (b) Standing and walking may worsen the break; (d) Lifting her up may displace the break.

PGI Exam Trap: She is asked to stand and walk to test the leg.

5-Second Recall: Keep her still and call for help at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Short and turned out means keep still.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a crush injury to the leg notes that his urine is dark and his pulse is rising. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and wait for the ward round
option_2: Hold his fluids to rest the kidneys
option_3: Ask him to walk to test the leg
option_4: Report it and give fluids as ordered
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Report it and give fluids as ordered

Clinical Rationale: Dark urine with a rising pulse after a crush injury points to muscle breakdown harming the kidneys, so it is reported and fluids are given.

Key Clue: dark urine with a rising pulse after a crush injury

Priority Principle: Rhabdomyolysis

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for the round risks the kidneys; (b) Holding fluids lets the kidneys be harmed more; (c) Walking strains the injured leg.

PGI Exam Trap: Fluids are held back to rest the kidneys.

5-Second Recall: Report it and give fluids as ordered.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dark urine after a crush means give fluids.
